# sv0cov: source-based code coverage for sv0

## purpose

**sv0cov** is a new standalone product (planned repo `sv0-toolchain/sv0cov`,
pinned as the `sv0cov/` submodule). It measures execution against original
`.sv0` source constructs, with one coverage truth across generated-C/native
execution and `.sv0b` execution on `sv0vm`.

It is **specification-first**. The governing document is:

- `~/Documents/project-specs/sv0cov/SPEC.md`: spec version `0.1.73-draft`
  (audit 2026-09-13; amended 2026-09-24 for D-1, DEC-086 / §15.6; amended
  2026-09-25 for D-3/D-6/D-7/D-8, DEC-087..090; amended 2026-09-27 for the
  `[tool.sv0cov]` config location, DEC-091). 91 accepted decisions, none open.

This file is the meta-repo planning **hub**: strategy, the observed gaps
between the spec's audit baseline and the current pins, open decisions, and the
release ladder. The trackable slice index is **`task/sv0cov-checklist.Rmd`**
(`CV-###`). Closure authority is `SPEC.md` (§31 release gates, §29
acceptance scenarios, §39 definition of done) plus these two files.

Like sv0-strings, sv0cov is a SPEC-governed product rather than a toolchain
milestone. It is therefore absent from the milestone table and
`task/milestone-orientation.json`.

## current state (2026-10-24)

- **F0, R0 and R0.1 are closed** (F0 2026-10-08, R0 2026-10-17, R0.1
  2026-10-24; gate reviews below). R1 (`4xx` slices in the checklist) is

- sv0cov is the `sv0cov/` submodule; the root policy

- Spec status: **Draft governing specification**. SPEC amendments owed by

## ownership (SPEC §3.1)

| Concern | Owner |
|---|---|
| Source syntax and semantics, bytecode contract, `coverage` attribute namespace | `sv0doc` |
| Planning, source regions, lowering provenance, C + VM instrumentation, map emission | `sv0c` |
| `.sv0b` loading, `COVER_HIT` execution, VM-side counters and profile flush | `sv0vm` |
| Merge, indexed evidence, reports, policy, public CLI, schemas, diagnostic registry | `sv0cov` |
| Submodule pin, `compatibility/sv0cov.json`, `./scripts/sv0 coverage` namespace | `sv0-toolchain` |

## observed gaps against current pins

The spec audited revisions from 2026-09-07 (§3.2). The pins are now the
`v0.1.0` release (meta `c7a72e2`). Re-checked 2026-09-24:

| # | Spec assumption | Observed now | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| G-1 | `sv0vm-v2-typed` is an existing container with sections (§15.2, §15.4); F0-G4 required v2 parity (before 0.1.71). | **No v2 container exists.** `sv0vm` (SML, ~1.6k lines) has one format (`formatVersion = 1`: header, strings, funcs, code; no sections). v2 is defined only by the separate, unimplemented `project-specs/sv0vm-implementation-expand/SPEC.md` (target R0.6 of a six-language VM program). | **Resolved by D-1 = A:** v2 staged to R1 (§15.6). |
| G-2 | sv0c computes SHA-256 (source digests, point IDs, fragment IDs, `map_id`). | **No SHA-256 anywhere** in sv0c, the C runtime, or sv0vm. M5 crypto `M5-S-040a/b` (SHA-256) is `todo`. | Planner map emission is blocked. **Decision D-2.** |
| G-3 | Parser skips attributes (§3.3 item 9). | **Resolved by CV-301/CV-302 (2026-10-17).** sv0doc has `attributed_statement` and the `coverage` page; sv0c's front-end pass `lib/attributes.sv0` keeps every attribute in a side table keyed by the annotated construct's first token, validates `coverage`, and strips attributes before the parser (which still reads `#[extern_c]` itself). | Exclusion effects are CV-305. |
| G-4 | Lexer discards comments (§3.3 item 10). | **Resolved by CV-304 (2026-10-18).** The lexer still drops comments; sv0c's pre-lex pass `lib/directives.sv0` scans each source unit for `// sv0cov:` directives (string-, character- and nested-comment-aware) and keeps a directive table with spans, reasons, start/end pairing and the code after each `ignore-next`. | Resolution to constructs and the exclusion effect are CV-305. |
| G-5 | Spans carry file + line/col + byte offsets. | `Span` fields are `i32`. Project mode concatenates every `.sv0` into one TU (`link_project_concat_sources_*`), so offsets are concat-relative. Columns are byte-based, not Unicode-scalar. | Planner needs a concat-offset → (logical path, file-relative byte) side table plus a scalar-column computation. |
| G-6 | IR lacks coverage provenance. | Still true (`ir.sv0` `Instr` has no span; the enum payload ceiling is 4). | Hit placement uses a new `Instr` variant keyed to a side table. |
| G-7 | Opcode 119 is free. | **Free** in sv0vm (118 = `RETURN_SLOTS`; next is 128) and unallocated in the expansion spec's registry. That spec says every unlisted opcode "SHALL fail", so 119 must also be registered there. | Needs a cross-spec note. |
| G-8 | A managed spawn-and-exec process API exists (§14.2.2). | **sv0 has no process API** in the language, the C runtime, or the VM. The runtime entry is `sv0_runtime_init(argc, argv)`. Contract failure is `exit(1)` from inline header helpers. | The process-lifecycle requirements reduce to fork-handler guards plus a flush hook. **Decision D-4.** |
| G-9 | CPython launcher rejects shims (§20.6.4). | This dev host resolves `python3.13`/`python3.14` through **pyenv shims**, which the launcher's `sys.executable` equality rejects. | The local launcher will fail closed here by design. Dev work needs a real interpreter first on `PATH`. |
| G-10 | Contract dispositions `runtime_checked` / `statically_verified` / `disabled` / `unsupported`. | **Resolved by CV-306 (2026-10-18).** Mapped as planned: contract mode disabled → `disabled`, model-only (`old`/`forall`/`exists`) → `unsupported`, a clause whose line `sv0 verify` proved (verified mode) → `statically_verified` with evidence `sv0c:smt:<kind>:<line>`, else `runtime_checked`. Two gaps found and closed on the way (D-23): `assert` and `loop_invariant` were never checked at runtime, and an `ensures` was skipped by an early `return` inside an `if` or loop. | sv0vm `getenv` (builtin 19) added 2026-10-18, so AC-106 runs on both backends. |

Decision: `fmt_sv0.py` refuses that layout with `file:line:col` at the attribute and leaves the file unchanged (`--check` fails too); it never invents an indentation. | ~~D-16~~ | CV-304 | **Resolved 2026-10-18 (owner).** SPEC 19.4 lists malformed directives among the failures of compilation "in coverage mode". Owed: a SPEC 19.4 note (stricter than, and compatible with, the current text). | Was: ignore directives in ordinary builds and validate them only under `--coverage`. |
| ~~D-17~~ | CV-304 | **Resolved 2026-10-18 (owner).** SPEC 19.3 gives the exact grammar but not what happens to near-misses. Decision: any line or block comment whose text, after the opener and spaces, starts with `sv0cov:` in any case is a directive attempt and must be spelled exactly `// sv0cov: ...` alone on its line, else `COV3201` (`//sv0cov:`, `// SV0COV:`, `/// sv0cov:`, `/* sv0cov: */` all fail), mirroring the attribute namespace rule; prose without the colon stays ordinary. Normative in sv0doc `attributes/coverage.md` §6. Owed: a SPEC 19.3 note. | Was: only comments beginning exactly `// sv0cov:` are directives; everything else is an ordinary comment. |
| ~~D-18~~ | CV-304 | **Resolved 2026-10-18 (owner).** SPEC 19.3 says start/end regions "MUST be properly nested", while COV-EXC-024 makes a wholly subsumed nested exclusion redundant. Decision: regions do not nest; a directive inside an open region, or between an `ignore-next` and its construct, is `COV3203`; an `ignore-end` without a start or a start never closed in its file is `COV3201`. Owed: a SPEC 19.3 note replacing "properly nested" with "not nested". | Was: allow nested regions and leave redundancy to CV-305. |
| ~~D-19~~ | CV-305 | **Resolved 2026-10-18 (owner).** SPEC 11.1 makes every excluded point uncounted, yet ordinary regions read excluded outcomes (the body of a `branch_off` decision is counted as its `true`; the code after an excluded `if` that returns as `entry − if.true`). Decision: such an outcome is observed by a counted `synthetic_support` point of kind `region` (the branch's span and entity, discriminator `support:<kind>:<outcome>`, hit where the outcome would be); the excluded outcome stays uncounted and the ordinary expression names the support point. Fits SPEC 11.1 ("counted exactly when the canonical plan needs a runtime observation") and the current sv0cov reader. No SPEC note needed; recorded in sv0cov `docs/planning-conventions.md`. | Was: keep excluded outcomes counted (contradicts SPEC 11.1/16.3.4). |
| ~~D-20~~ | CV-305 | **Resolved 2026-10-18 (owner).** Lowering hits a decision's outcomes at consecutive counters (outcome k = first + k). Decision: when any outcome of an excluded decision is needed, every reachable outcome of that decision gets a support point, so lowering is unchanged; an unread support point costs one counter and enters no denominator. | Was: support only the needed outcomes (a tier-2 `lowering.sv0` change with golden regeneration). |
| ~~D-21~~ | CV-305 | **Resolved 2026-10-18 (owner).** SPEC 19.3: `ignore-next` applies to "the next executable source construct", undefined inside an expression. Decision: the smallest planned construct starting at the next code (past attributes, `use`/`module` declarations and code-free items): an item or statement whole, else an `if` or `match` expression; anything else (an operand, a call) is `COV1021` until CV-307 plans expression-level points. Never silently widened. Owed: a SPEC 19.3 note. | Was: widen to the enclosing statement. |
| ~~D-22~~ | CV-305 | **Resolved 2026-10-18 (owner).** A construct that only partly overlaps an `ignore-start` region: `COV3201`; both directives must stand between the items or statements of one block (SPEC 19.4 "an exclusion spanning source ownership boundaries"); an empty region is `COV1021`. Owed: a SPEC 19.3 note. | Was: clip to whole constructs silently. |
| ~~D-23~~ | CV-306 | **Resolved 2026-10-18 (owner).** sv0doc says `assert expr` panics when false (keywords 1.12) and `loop_invariant` is a runtime check at the start of every iteration (contracts 1.4, 3.1), but sv0c only evaluated asserts and dropped invariants. Decision: implement the enforcement in CV-306 on both backends, so all four clause kinds can be `runtime_checked`: an invariant is checked at the head of every iteration (so once more on exit); `--contract-mode=disabled` strips both; verified mode strips a proven invariant. Failures print `sv0 contract violation: <kind> failed in <fn>` (VM: `<kind> failed: <fn>`), exit 1. It exposed one real bug in sv0-mathlib (`stats_sorted_f64`'s invariant `last >= 0` is false for an empty input; fixed to `last >= 0 - 1`). | Was: classify assert/loop_invariant `unsupported` and enforce later. |
| D-5 | CV-233 | Which toolchain entry point does `sv0cov run` use to build? | Default: `./scripts/sv0 native-compile` / `vm-native-compile` with the new `--coverage=instrument` flag. This is non-normative; recorded rather than asked. |

## cross-spec conflicts with the installed-toolchain spec (2026-09-27)

`project-specs/sv0-toolchain-interface-and-distribution/SPEC.md` (0.1.0-draft,
hub `task/sv0-toolchain-interface-distribution.Rmd`) changes three things
sv0cov depends on. Nothing here blocks F0, but R0 configuration and the
build entry point (D-5) each needed an owner decision. **All three were resolved
2026-09-27** (maintainer accepted the recommendations):

| # | Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| X-1 | sv0cov config is a root `[coverage]` table in `sv0.toml` (§18.2, DEC-048/051). Manifest v1 rejects unknown root tables and reserves `[tool.<name>]` for companions (TID §9.8, MAN-002). | **Resolved:** SPEC `0.1.73-draft` DEC-091 moves the config to `[tool.sv0cov]`; nothing else changes. CV-2xx config slices use `[tool.sv0cov]`. |
| X-2 | `--coverage=off\|map\|instrument` / `--coverage-map` (CV-106) are not in the installed `sv0c` BR1 grammar, where unknown options fail (TID CCLI-006). | **Resolved:** TID `0.1.1-draft` DEC-062 / CCLI-015. Release-mode `sv0c` rejects them; they stay repo-driver / development-build options until `sv0 cov` ships as a same-prefix companion (TID DEC-031; `TID-902`). D-5's default (`./scripts/sv0 native-compile` / `vm-native-compile`) stays valid because repository adapters remain (TID §22.2). |
| X-3 | TID's installed tools must not need Python at run time (DEC-005). sv0cov is Python through R1. | Consistent: `sv0 cov` is deferred past BR1 (TID §12.1). No sv0cov change. |

| DV-6 | The F0 reader adds all contexts into one aggregate; per-context counts are R0. | `sv0cov/src/sv0cov/resolve.py` |
| DV-7 | G9: only portable CRC32C implementations exist, so there is no accelerated one to test. | this table |

## R01-G6 performance-host plan (CV-315, SPEC §24.1, DEC-087)

**Accountable path (owner decision, 2026-10-24): all four R1 performance
classes produce their R1 evidence as `managed-ci-recorded` campaigns under
the DEC-087 managed-CI exception.** No dedicated host is procured or
provisioned now. The accountable owner for every class is the sole
maintainer. R1-G9 is then satisfied only together with one exception
record per gate (COV-PERF-023/024).

**Why not dedicated.** The only owned machine, an Apple M3 Mac (arm64,
8 logical CPUs, 8 GiB, internal APFS SSD, macOS 26.6.2), meets the CPU floor
but not the 32 GiB floor of a `reference-dedicated` host. It runs the harness
only at stage `local-development`. The managed runners below are shared
virtual machines below every dedicated floor, so they cannot become
`reference-dedicated` hosts either.

Observed on the provisional campaign of 2026-10-19 (sv0cov
`perf-provisional.yml`, run 39264665243, all four green):

| Class | Runner label | Observed CPU | Logical CPUs | Memory | Virtualization | Dedicated floors met |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linux x86-64 | `ubuntu-24.04` | Intel Xeon 6973P-C | 4 | 15.6 GiB | VM | no (CPUs, memory, isolation) |
| Linux arm64 | `ubuntu-24.04-arm` | unknown at the time (probe fixed in CV-315) | 4 | 15.6 GiB | VM | no |
| macOS x86-64 | `macos-15-intel` | Intel Core i7-8700B | 4 | 14.0 GiB | VM | no |
| macOS arm64 | `macos-15` | Apple M1 (Virtual) | 3 | 7.0 GiB | VM | no |

**Descriptor.** `bench/harness.py host` already emits every SPEC §24.1 field.
On managed runners these stay `unknown` by nature and go into each class's
exception record: physical CPU count (Linux), power/performance mode,
thermal and throttling state, storage device class, non-overcommit and
background-load ceiling, scheduler affinity. CV-315 fixed the fields that
were observable but recorded as unknown: the toolchain revision (never
passed by the workflow), the Linux arm64 CPU model, and the filesystem.

**What each exception record names** (SPEC §24.1, DEC-087): host class,
provider and runner label, runner image, observed hardware, every missing
descriptor field, the measured variance of the gated fixtures, and the risk
accepted. Budgets, correctness, per-fixture ceilings and the no-pooling and
no-compensation rules are unchanged; a campaign's results are never labelled
dedicated-reference evidence.

**No pooling across observed hardware.** The harness series key includes the
observed CPU model, so a runner that moves to other hardware starts a new
series. A gate is evaluated from one series only, and a hardware change
during a campaign invalidates that campaign for the class.

**What CV-410 must build on this plan:**

- a `managed-ci-recorded` harness stage (today: `managed-ci-provisional`,
  `reference-dedicated`, `local-development`), whose bundles may feed R1-G9
  only with their exception records;
- the exception-record artifact and its schema, and the budget evaluator
  that refuses a gate without one;
- a recorded-campaign workflow over the complete frozen corpus (the
  provisional workflow runs only the 1M-pair ingest fixture), at least three
  complete campaigns per class for the measured variance;
- the pending corpus fixtures (`region-large` exceeds the native compiler's
  Vec-handle table).

**Transition, if dedicated hardware appears.** A class moves to
`reference-dedicated` only on a host meeting every floor (8 logical CPUs,
32 GiB, local SSD, native architecture, fixed power mode, no overcommit,
complete descriptor), after three complete overlap campaigns on the same
toolchain, corpus, configuration and protocol (COV-PERF-025). Historical
managed results are never converted. Replacing a dedicated host repeats the
descriptor, overlap and four-host rebaseline (COV-PERF-026).

**Risks accepted, and their triggers:**

- *Runner retirement.* GitHub has been retiring Intel macOS images. If
  `macos-15-intel` (or a successor Intel label) is unavailable before the R1
  campaign, the macOS x86-64 class has no path. The trigger is a deprecation
  notice for the label. The fallbacks are an owner-supplied Intel Mac that meets
  every dedicated floor (it then follows the overlap procedure), or a SPEC
  amendment for that class. This is decided then, not now.
- *Small, shared runners* (3-4 vCPU, 7-16 GiB) make the concurrency and
  memory budgets the most exposed. Their variance is measured and recorded,
  never averaged away.
- *Scheduled provisional runs* failed until the B9 variance-unit fix
  (2026-10-19). The on-demand run after it passed on all four classes; the
  next scheduled run confirms the schedule.

## tracks

- **Track P: protocol freeze** (sv0cov repo, pure Python, **no toolchain
  changes; can start immediately**). Canonical JSON, point-ID preimage, closed
  schemas + generated validators, raw-profile codec + CRC32C, VM binding/COVR
  codecs, diagnostic registry, compatibility/version/doctor schemas, semantic
  fixture corpus. These become the oracle every other track tests against
  (SPEC §28.3).
- **Track U: upstream enablement** (sv0doc / sv0c / sv0vm). Bytecode
  revision, SHA-256, source-unit table, `--coverage` modes, the planner,
  lowering provenance, C emission + native runtime, VM emission + SML
  interpreter support. v2 moves to R1 (CV-46x).
- **Track T: tool** (sv0cov repo). Readers, indexed model, merge, config, CLI,
  reports, policy.
- **Track R: root integration** (sv0-toolchain). Submodule, compatibility
  policy, fixed launcher, `./scripts/sv0 coverage`, toolchain doctor.
- **Track Q: quality + release.** Fuzzing, portability, performance, supply
  chain, release engineering.

## working rules

- **Red first** (SPEC §30): every implementation slice is preceded by fixtures
  or tests that fail for the intended reason. Expected coverage maps are
  hand-reviewed. Generated C, bytecode, LCOV, and Cobertura are never the
  oracle (§28.3).
- **Cross-repo slices** record authority, producer/consumer versions, update
  order, conformance test, and rollback (§8.3, COV-GOV-006).
- Compiler slices follow `30-sv0c-compiler-boundaries.mdc` and the test-suite
  bar: every sv0c/sv0vm change ships gated tests on both backends where
  applicable.
- Cite `COV-*` requirement IDs and `AC-*` scenarios in commits.

## repo layout (SPEC §8.1)

```text
sv0cov/
├── README.md  LICENSE  LICENSE-APACHE  LICENSE-MIT  LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt  REUSE.toml
├── pyproject.toml  uv.lock
├── scripts/{sv0cov,sv0cov-python}
├── src/sv0cov/{cli,formats,merge,report,policy,model,_generated/validators}/
├── runtime/{c,protocol}/        # native collection runtime (C11), byte protocol docs
├── registries/diagnostics-v1.json
├── resources/doctor/doctor-r1-smoke.sv0
├── schemas/                     # canonical Draft 2020-12 closed-profile schemas
├── tests/{fixtures,conformance,integration,differential,vendor}/
└── docs/
```

Placement choice: the native runtime **source** is owned by sv0cov
(`runtime/c/`, shipped in the wheel per COV-PKG-005) and linked by sv0c's
native build. The VM counter path lives in sv0vm.
